# Score-blind inventory contract

Produce one JSON object with exactly motion, routes, sections, moves, coverageAudit, speakerAttributionReview, selectionBalanceAudit, publicationCapacityAudit. No ratings, totals, winner, critiques, tags or AI contribution. The controller adds identity and exact source excerpts mechanically.

Read this plan and the complete maintained reader through bounded untruncated calls, including every source event, every source restriction and all shared blocks. E labels are ONE-BASED; startEvent/endEvent are ZERO-BASED. Do not open other debates, assessments, peer outputs, credentials, session logs or external sources. Pinned checker source is a tool input, not mandatory reading.

## Identity and scope

Motion: Is the physical resurrection of Jesus the best explanation for Christianity's origins?
Pro: Jonathan McLatchie. Con: Paulogia.

The title asks whether physical resurrection was required. Both speakers explicitly develop comparative explanations, but their adopted burdens differ: McLatchie defends the best explanation and rejects deductive necessity; Paulogia challenges necessity and superiority, proposes a sincere-mistake/oral-development possibility and ultimately favors a natural explanation. Preserve those distinctions in route bridges, move descriptions and reply links. Never turn McLatchie into an advocate of logical necessity or require Paulogia to prove one uniquely identified natural historical cause merely to challenge the offered inference.

Obey every assessment-source-notes.md and source-lock.json restriction. Assess only both openings, their direct debate and both final argument summaries in retained intervals. Audience Q&A, host logistics, banter, promotions and outro are excluded without credit, penalty or missing-reply inference. No substantive moderator exception is needed. Do not import the Q&A miracle case, harmonization examples or outside scholarship. Supplied chapter titles are unreliable; follow spoken handoffs and exact scope intervals.

## Routes and sections

Exactly two routes {side,speaker,bridges}. Each bridges array has 3–7 unique {bridgeId,tier,description} objects: exactly one motion tier, at least one central and one subsidiary. IDs globally unique and owned by their side. Describe burdens, not achievements.

Use 4–7 coherent topical sections {sectionId,title,weightPercent,rationale}. Unique descriptive lowercase-slug IDs; never s1/s2. Positive integer weights total 100 and reflect motion-level importance before judgment. Each section contains genuine moves from both sides. Three per side is ordinary, four maximum. Every fourth requires a source-specific distinct/nonmergeable/independently-assessable justification. Preserve chronology and response meaning; do not manufacture symmetry or omit load-bearing material for display. Group a coherent paired exchange together when setting semantic sections.

## Moves

Select 8–48 load-bearing moves in chronological order. Each object contains:
- moveId: unique descriptive lowercase slug, never m1/m2.
- side, speaker, sectionId: exact locked identities.
- moveKind: constructive or reply.
- claim, warrant, inference: separate faithful descriptions, no ratings.
- startEvent,endEvent: inclusive ZERO-BASED indices; smallest complete contiguous supporting passage.
- sourceSpanSelectionRationale: source-specific boundaries, at least 40 characters; a span over 2200 source characters needs a compelling complete-argument rationale of at least 100 characters.
- quoteEligibleExactSpans: zero to two exact complete 3–18 word source substrings, [] if unsuitable. At least one suitable complete-thought candidate per side in the inventory. Never truncate a concession, qualification, referent or conclusion. Never silently fix caption wording in a quote.
- attributionConfidence: high/medium/low; attributionRationale; audioVerificationReason.
- importance: integer 1–3; importanceRationale based on burden, not quality.
- burdenContact: {bridgeId,tier,rationale} owned by this side.
- respondsToIds: earlier selected IDs or [] for constructive moves.
- responseComponents: replies require {targetMoveId,description} for every actual selected target; constructive moves use [].

Retain load-bearing targets of selected replies. Repetition is not a new move; new distinctions and answers matter. Both closings must be reviewed, though pure recapitulation need not create additional scored moves. Keep spans narrow. Mixed turns may remain in a necessary contiguous span only when exact scored ownership is unambiguous, with the attribution audit explicitly excluding interjected words. Quotes must be wholly the assigned participant's words. Source restrictions identify recognition-corrupted clauses: none may justify ratings, concessions or alleged contradictions. Any selected material uncertainty that persists must be below high confidence and will require audio verification. Seven auxiliary checks have occurred, not direct human listening or diarization.

## Audits

coverageAudit accounts for every major retained line with selected IDs and source-specific reasons for omitted repetition, logistics or lesser material. Account for all excluded intervals without scoring them. Preserve concessions and qualifications; review both final summaries.

speakerAttributionReview records actual handoffs, explicit addressees, first-person continuity, mixed spans and uncertainty. Describe the exact basis rather than blanket high-confidence claims. Never claim to have listened or verified passages outside the supplied checks.

selectionBalanceAudit: {thresholds:{totalAbsoluteDifference:3,sectionAbsoluteDifference:2},totals:{pro:N,con:N,absoluteDifference:N},sections:[{sectionId,pro:N,con:N,absoluteDifference:N}],rationaleRequired:boolean,rationale:string}. Sections in locked order. Rationale required when total difference >=3 or any section difference >=2; identify why asymmetric selections are load-bearing.

publicationCapacityAudit: {maximumSelectedMovesPerSidePerSection:4,sections:[{sectionId,pro:N,con:N,withinCapacity:boolean,fourthRowRequired:boolean,fourthRowAuthorized:boolean,rationale:string}],allSectionsWithinCapacity:boolean,allFourthRowsPreauthorized:boolean}. fourthRowRequired means either side has four; fourthRowAuthorized true for ordinary rows or justified fourth rows. Controller independently recomputes counts and flags.

## One submission

Confirm the execution plan's absolute output destination. Read the complete packet; send a complete-reading checkpoint and WAIT for controller authentication before authoring. Prepare the candidate in memory, run the pinned checker through stdin, then send the exact JSON bytes through stdin to handoff hold. No draft file. Controller inspects the entire candidate and alone releases its exact first save. Never self-approve, edit a submission, create subagents, make paid calls, inspect peers or open session logs. One fresh context, one attempt, zero automatic retries. Unsaved corrections remain in this same context and attempt.

# Assessment source notes

1. Assess only both ten-minute openings, the two participants’ direct debate before audience Q&A, and both final argument summaries. Approximate ranges are 2:26–1:36:18 and 2:03:51–2:06:20, excluding handoffs, banter and resource promotions. The retained intervals are authoritative. Exclude every audience question and its replies, introductions, host logistics and outro. No credit, penalty, inferred concession or failure-to-reply inference may depend on excluded material. Full-source access is for scope and contextual audit only.

2. The publisher frames the event as whether physical resurrection was required for Christianity to develop. The neutral assessment question compares the explanations actually defended: Is the physical resurrection of Jesus the best explanation for Christianity's origins? McLatchie explicitly disclaims logical necessity and argues comparative probability; Paulogia begins with non-necessity, then challenges comparative superiority and ultimately favors a natural explanation. Preserve both adopted burdens. Do not call McLatchie an advocate of deductive necessity or treat mere possibility as establishing Paulogia’s positive preference. Do not impose proof of one uniquely identified historical cause on a critic who mainly challenges the offered inference.

3. McLatchie presents a maximal-data or Paley-style cumulative case: mundane confirmations support proximity, information and truthfulness; sufficiently detailed unembellished eyewitness claims resist honest mistake; costly proclamation supports sincerity. He explicitly allows combinations of explanatory categories. Paulogia’s core challenge concerns whether the Gospel narratives reach eyewitness testimony at all and whether historical kernels warrant the miraculous portions. Distinguish these steps and do not omit the conditional premise.

4. Both agree that the minimal-facts material in 1 Corinthians 15 alone leaves the nature of the experiences underdetermined. McLatchie does not defend minimal facts as sufficient; his reliance on Gospel detail is deliberate. Paulogia allows hypothetical historical kernels, including Philip’s origin, without conceding the Gospel authors were eyewitnesses, personally knew eyewitnesses, or wrote uniformly reliable accounts. Conditional grants are not adopted beliefs.

5. McLatchie offers undesigned coincidences, unexplained allusions and consistent characterization as different but cumulative considerations. Paulogia proposes shared oral tradition, literary dependence, genuine historical kernels, elaboration and coincidence rather than a single rigid written source. The Star Wars analogy is an illustration of story interconnection without truth, not an asserted historical cause of Christian texts. Treat all historical and textual claims as arguments made here, not externally verified facts.

6. The discrepancy exchange has two explicitly distinguished effects in McLatchie’s account: a genuine error detracts from reliability while increasing independence. Do not attribute the claim that discrepancies only confirm reliability. He allows partial dependence with partial independence and distinguishes well-informed testimony from an infallible document. Paulogia questions discrimination between those accounts and ordinary story development. Do not import the audience-Q&A harmonization of Mary Magdalene into their direct exchange.

7. The automatic captions and auxiliary recognition remain uncertain in several isolated clauses. Around E1419–E1441 (49 minutes), do not infer an inconsistency or concession from the ambiguous do/don’t wording about a mega-gospel or common oral tradition. At E1660–E1662 the corrupted polarity about honest mistake is unusable; the subsequent complete E1667–E1682 conditional states that such mistake is unlikely. At E2059–E2068, the auxiliary check recovers McLatchie’s ability to give specific examples, Peter and John; do not score the caption “we can’t give specific examples” as a concession. Source claims elsewhere remain assessable; no deduction may rest on these recognition defects.

8. McLatchie’s persecution argument is explicitly more modest than all twelve died rather than recanting. He names Peter, Paul, the two Jameses and later John; he concedes that Nero’s political scapegoating weakens an inference from the specific executions and that opportunities to recant are not established. The claim is voluntary risks, hardship and general persecution support sincerity, not prove it. Stephen is offered as contextual evidence, not necessarily a resurrection witness. Paulogia accepts a general persecution context and that John requires an account, while asking for the witnesses’ specific claims and independent support.

9. Paulogia’s “Acts aside” question is hypothetical; McLatchie refuses that exclusion because he defends Acts and also mentions Clement. Do not describe the latter as conceding there is literally no other cited source. Preserve the distinction between reliability as authentic testimony and the truth of its subject matter. McLatchie expressly agrees that confirming mundane facts does not logically entail resurrection, and explains why he still finds those facts evidentially relevant.

10. Paulogia’s skepticism about miracle testimony is qualified in the late direct exchange: he does not claim philosophical naturalism, and allows that medical documentation could increase a modern miracle claim’s significance. His strongest testimony-only language is later expressed as uncertainty about his own threshold; he also doubts Gospel independence and whether an event’s attribution follows from many reports. McLatchie argues from the purpose of divine signs, religious context and increasing testimonial quantity/quality. The caption “can be a significant objection” at E2660 is missing a negation: the auxiliary check confirms “can’t.” Do not score the corrupted positive claim.

11. The Barbara Snyder multiple-sclerosis report, Shroud of Turin, John Douglas/McGrew criteria, alien technology, dying/rising religions, audience probability formula and final divine-salvation answer occur in excluded audience Q&A. Do not credit or criticize either side using those answers or the subsequent reaction video. McLatchie’s pre-Q&A references to contemporary miracles and other apologetic categories are retained only at the level presented there; do not import detailed cases from Q&A or outside sources.

12. Both final summaries repeat the main positions and must be reviewed; score a closing as a distinct move only for genuinely load-bearing argumentative work, not repetition. McLatchie’s closing repeats comparative probability rather than certainty; Paulogia reiterates non-necessity, the single sincere mistaken person hypothesis, his objection to global reliability transfer, and a naturalistic preference. Do not penalize McLatchie for lacking a subsequent chance to answer the last closing.

13. Public automatic captions were supplemented by seven targeted automated audio-to-text checks. Neither direct human listening nor automatic speaker diarization was performed. Canonical caption words and timestamps remain unchanged. Names and technical terms often contain recognition errors; do not quote or penalize them. Do not silently repair exact quotations. Any remaining selected material uncertainty must be below high confidence and receive required audio verification before adjudication.

14. Featured quotations must be exact complete 3–18 word standalone thoughts from the locked canonical source, with clear referents and necessary qualifications. Both final summaries provide complete candidate thoughts. A different complete excerpt is required if the necessary qualification exceeds the length ceiling. No invented completion words or misleadingly truncated concession.

The dialogue begins with McLatchie questioning “required” at E709; their alternating prompts, first-person replies and explicit addressees establish the turns. Cameron Bertuzzi’s retained-area intervention around E2524–E2530 is logistical and is excluded. E3509–E3529 is McLatchie’s final argument; E3551–E3578 is Paulogia’s final argument. Auxiliary checks confirm argument continuity but are not diarization. Distinguish mixed caption events at handoffs and never quote another speaker’s words as the move owner’s.
